target_customer: Independent and chain restaurants wanting takeout and delivery orders by web and phone
problem: Restaurants lose phone and online orders and depend on commission-heavy marketplaces.
business_model: B2B SaaS for restaurants, later an AI phone answering product called Greet; pricing not found

founders.name: Adam Sandler
founders.background_notes: YC bio: trying to make something people want. Same name as the actor; no link implied.

founders.name: David Xiao
founders.background_notes: Described as CEO and co-founder in a Medium article seen in search.

exit.reason: Cause not public. The company site bensen.ai now shows a parked domain.

technical_complexity.rationale: Voice ordering on Alexa and Google Assistant and phone answering needed speech handling and POS integration, standard for the time.

defensibility.rationale: Restaurant integrations created some switching cost, but ordering platforms were crowded and voice tech was commoditizing.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large ordering platforms owned the restaurant relationship; no dated source on their reaction to Bensen.

market_need_then: PYMNTS (2019) covered voice ordering at quick service restaurants as an emerging channel. No Bensen-specific demand data found.

branding.domain_note: Used bensen.ai, an .ai domain. It is now a parked placeholder.

brand_strength.rationale: No press on the brand found. The name Bensen was not explained by sources.

pivots.from: Online and phone ordering for restaurant takeout and delivery
pivots.to: Voice assistant ordering and an AI phone receptionist (Greet)
pivots.why: Not stated; coverage from PYMNTS and Medium shows the later products.

outcome_analysis: Bensen began as restaurant online and phone ordering and moved toward voice ordering and the Greet AI phone product, reportedly serving hundreds of restaurants per a Medium article seen in search. Funding found is a small seed of about 150 thousand dollars from databases. The company is now inactive and its domain parked, but no source gives the cause.
notes: The seed round rests on CB Insights and Village (RiverPark named only by Village); startup-seeker says undisclosed. Medium article returned 403 on fetch, so its claims come from search snippets and are unverified. Dated competitor sources near the batch naming rivals were not found; Olo, ChowNow and Toast are known incumbents but only undated or recent pages were found, so the list is empty.
